origin: the feet of this body are mesh vertices of Tarsus5, not pads. Every evaluation so far measured the contact of a mesh corner against the floor, and the friction scan showed that raising mu alone saturates at slip ~0.99. This round replaces the foot contact with a declared spherical pad geom per leg.

derived_body.change_1: one sphere geom named <LEG>Tarsus5_pad added inside each <LEG>Tarsus5 body, radius 0.01 native units, centre placed so the sphere's lowest point coincides with the mesh's lowest vertex (so the standing height and key pose are unchanged)
derived_body.change_2: the six Tarsus5 mesh geoms get contype=0 conaffinity=0, so the pads are the only foot contacts
unchanged: all other geom types, sizes and positions
actuator gains, force limits, timestep, gravity
nothing is written to the frozen XML
derived_body.invariants_to_verify: nq 49, nv 48, nu 42, nmesh 71, neq 0, joint ranges and body masses bit-identical to the frozen model; ngeom 72 -> 78

friction: sliding friction mu = 1.5 on every geom at runtime (the best value from the friction scan), declared as friction-derived
controller: the same full-42-joint PPO recipe as the stand-pose run: start from the solved stand pose, base network MODEL_MEASURED_STAND as a faded prior, reward v4, adhesion channel on during training, 64 updates with a gate check every 16
evaluation: cold-start 4 s and assist-then-release 4 s, grip on (derived channel) and grip off (frozen-body-style comparison, but with the pad body and mu 1.5, therefore also derived), full and steady windows, per-leg slip measured on the pad geoms
gates: unchanged: support mean >= 0.90, non-foot max <= 0.05W*4, COM min >= 1.20, slip max <= 0.50, forward >= 0.05
labelling: derived body + derived friction + replacement ANN; none of this is frozen-body acceptance and none of it is connectome or brain output
accounting: pad geometry, radius, positions, the old and new XML sha256, the invariant check, native steps, and every metric including failures are recorded
